definitions.explanation: the act of moving a plant to a new pot or location

examples.japanese: {観葉植物|かんようしょくぶつ}の{植|う}え{替|か}えをした。
{春|はる}は{植|う}え{替|か}えに{良|よ}い{季節|きせつ}だ。
examples.english: Spring is a good season for repotting.

examples.japanese: {根|ね}が{詰|つ}まってきたので{植|う}え{替|か}えが{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: The roots are getting crowded, so repotting is needed.

notes:
{植|う}え{替|か}え refers to moving a plant to a new pot or location, typically to promote better growth.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {植|う}え{替|か}えをする: to do repotting
- {植|う}え{替|か}える: to repot (verb form)
- {植|う}え{替|か}えの{時期|じき}: repotting season

WHEN TO REPOT:
- {根詰|ねづ}まり: root-bound condition
- {鉢|はち}が{小|ちい}さくなった: pot has become too small
- {土|つち}が{古|ふる}くなった: soil has become old/depleted

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {移植|いしょく}: transplanting (more formal/technical; also used for organ transplants)
- {定植|ていしょく}: permanent planting (from seedbed to final location)

Spring is the most common time for {植|う}え{替|か}え, as plants recover more easily during the growing season.
